introduction-physics-and-the-law.core: Some workloads can't move fully to a region. Physics (single-digit-ms latency to factory machines, local data processing) and law (data residency, sovereignty) keep them on-premises or at the edge. Hybrid tools extend AWS APIs and management to those locations instead of running two disconnected worlds.

first_principles.problem: A factory's control system needs < 5 ms latency and a regulator requires data to stay in-country, where there's no AWS region.
truths: Laws can bind data to locations.
Two management planes double ops work.

analogy.title: A company opening a branch office under head-office rules
analogy.story: Local presence for speed and law, same procedures as headquarters.
analogy.breaks: Branches can act independently; Outposts depend on a link to the parent region for control.

example.title: Classifying workloads
flow: Factory PLC analytics, 2 ms → Outposts on site
Metro media rendering, 5 ms → Local Zone
Legacy on-prem servers → SSM hybrid activation

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Each constraint met with AWS tooling.

check.q: Name two reasons a workload can't move to an AWS region.
check.a: Latency requirements (physics) and data residency/sovereignty rules (law).

aws-outposts-cloud-in-a-box.core: Outposts are AWS-owned racks (or 1U/2U servers) installed in your data centre, running EC2, EBS, ECS/EKS, RDS, S3 on Outposts and more with the same APIs and console, managed by AWS as an extension of a parent region. They need a reliable service link to that region for control plane operations.

first_principles.problem: An on-prem workload must stay local but the team wants the same AWS tooling as in the cloud.
truths: Control plane stays in the region.
derivation: Create **subnets on the Outpost** in your VPC.

analogy.title: A franchise kiosk inside your building
analogy.story: Same products and processes as the main store, run by the franchise, in your space.
analogy.breaks: Kiosks restock from anywhere; Outposts capacity is fixed until AWS installs more hardware.

example.title: Low-latency manufacturing app
flow: Outpost rack in plant data centre
Local gateway to PLC network (1 ms)

check.q: What happens to Outposts control-plane operations if the service link to the region fails?
check.a: Running workloads continue, but control-plane actions (launching new instances, etc.) are unavailable until the link returns.

systems-manager-ssm-for-hybrid-environme.core: SSM manages non-AWS servers and VMs (on-prem, other clouds, edge) through hybrid activations: install the SSM Agent with an activation code and ID, and machines appear as managed nodes (mi-…). You get Session Manager, Run Command, Patch Manager, Inventory and State Manager on the same terms as EC2.

first_principles.problem: Hundreds of on-prem servers are patched and accessed with separate tools and shared SSH keys.
truths: IAM roles can govern hybrid nodes.
derivation: Create a **hybrid activation** with an IAM service role.

analogy.title: Adding contractors' tools to the company tool tracker
analogy.story: Every tool, wherever it lives, shows up in one system and follows the same checkout rules.
analogy.breaks: Tool trackers just track; SSM can execute commands and patch remotely.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Server patched and accessed like EC2.

code.text:
aws ssm create-activation --default-instance-name onprem --iam-role SSMServiceRole --registration-limit 200
# on the server:
sudo amazon-ssm-agent -register -code "<code>" -id "<id>" -region eu-west-1 && sudo systemctl restart amazon-ssm-agent

check.q: What prefix do hybrid managed nodes get in SSM?

choosing-the-right-hybrid-tool.core: Match the tool to the constraint: Local Zones for metro low latency without owning hardware; Outposts for on-premises AWS infrastructure; Snow family for disconnected or rugged edge and bulk data transfer; Greengrass for IoT edge compute; SSM for managing existing servers; Direct Connect/VPN for connectivity; EKS Anywhere/ECS Anywhere for container orchestration on your own hardware.

first_principles.problem: A team picks Outposts for a need that a Local Zone would satisfy at lower cost.
truths: Each tool solves a specific constraint.

analogy.title: Picking transport for a trip
analogy.story: Taxi, hire van, off-road vehicle or courier, depending on terrain and load.
analogy.breaks: Transport choices are per trip; hybrid commitments can last years.

example.title: Decision table
flow: Game streaming in LA → Local Zone
Hospital imaging must stay on site → Outposts
Ship with intermittent satellite → Snowball Edge

check.q: Which service fits a disconnected, rugged environment?
check.a: The AWS Snow family (e.g. Snowball Edge).
